terms.comment: One sent with a commission (lēgāre); also a general’s or a governor’s deputy (Lewis & Short). Traupman and Levi–Bini give it for an ambassador, Morgan–Owens for any diplomat.

terms.gloss: an envoy who speaks for his people
evidence: Liv. 1.15.5: Vejentēs pācem petītum ōrātōrēs Rōmam mittunt
terms.comment: The spokesman of an embassy (Lewis & Short); in Renaissance and modern Latin the usual title of an ambassador (Busbecq, Milton and Egger, in Morgan–Owens).

phrases.latin: eōs ipsōs quōs cernant lēgātōs nōn pinnīs sublīme ēlātōs Alpēs trānsgressōs
phrases.english: the very envoys they could see had not crossed the Alps lifted up on wings
